Calibrate Tucker3 via grid search

Source: R/calibration.R
calibrate_tucker3.Rd

Searches over rank combinations and time-series methods to find the best Tucker3 configuration. Supports two selection strategies: rolling-origin cross-validation ("cv", slower but more robust) or information criteria ("bic"/"aic", fast screening).

Usage

calibrate_tucker3(
  mx_array,
  years,
  ages,
  method = "coda",
  width = 5,
  h_val = 3,
  min_train = 12,
  rank_selection = c("cv", "bic", "aic"),
  cv_metric = c("mase", "mase_combined", "mase_trend")
)

Arguments

mx_array

3D array of mortality rates.

years

Integer vector of years.

ages

Integer vector of age-group starts.

method

"coda" or "direct".

width

Age-group width.

h_val

Validation horizon (used only for rank_selection = "cv").

min_train

Minimum training years (used only for rank_selection = "cv").

rank_selection

Character; "cv" (default) for rolling-origin cross-validation, "bic" or "aic" for information criterion based selection. When using IC, the ts_method is selected via a smaller CV using the best ranks.

cv_metric

Character; scoring metric for cross-validation. "mase" (default), "mase_combined", or "mase_trend". See resolve_cv_metric().

Value

Named list with R_A, R_B, R_C, ts_method, cv_score (or ic_value for BIC/AIC selection).
